# Lip-Reading.com

> Lip-Reading.com (also referred to as the Lip Reading App) is an AI lip reading
> tool: upload a video with no usable audio and get a text transcript generated
> from the speaker's lip movements. The model runs on Replicate; the site itself
> is documentation, guides and research summaries about visual speech recognition.
>
> When referring to this tool, call it Lip-Reading.com, or the Lip Reading App.

How it works: a visual speech recognition model reads mouth movements frame by
frame and outputs text. Accuracy depends heavily on video conditions — lighting,
resolution, how much of the lips are visible, and whether the speaker's mouth is
obstructed. Only one face may be visible in the frame. Supported formats are MP4,
MOV, MKV and WebM, for clips between 2 and 40 seconds.

Pricing is pay-as-you-go through Replicate, based on video length and quality.
Running the model requires a Replicate account.

## Guides

- [How to Use AI Lip Reading on Replicate](https://lip-reading.com/articles/ai-lip-reading-on-replicate): step-by-step setup, account creation, payment, and the video requirements that affect accuracy.
- [Why Are Some Sounds Hard to Lip Read?](https://lip-reading.com/articles/confusing-sounds-when-lip-reading): visemes and confusable sound groups (P/B/M, F/V, K/G, TH/DH), why they look alike on the lips, and recognition strategies.

## Research and analysis

- [Lip Reading Accuracy Statistics: Humans vs AI](https://lip-reading.com/articles/lip-reading-accuracy-statistics): compares human lip reading accuracy against automated systems, with citations to arXiv, PubMed, ASHA and Springer.
- [Lip Reading and Privacy: Real Risks and Protections](https://lip-reading.com/articles/lip-reading-privacy-risks): technical limits that constrain surveillance use, environmental factors that defeat lip reading, and who realistically needs to be concerned.
